findings.title: Frontline/production-floor staff reluctant to use app after shifts (adoption/culture, not a product defect)
findings.description: Gordon says office adoption is steady but production-floor workers (brewers, packaging, warehouse) don't want to open the app after a shift to work on training plans. Rotating shift schedules also make group sessions hard to schedule. By L54, Gordon explicitly frames this as 'a me-problem, not a you-problem' tied to workplace culture, not a tool defect, and doesn't ask for a product change.
findings.quote: they finish a shift, they don't want to open an app and work on their dog's training plan
findings.severity_reason: Not actionable as a product issue; customer attributes it to internal culture/adoption, not the software.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue covers adoption/culture friction; customer explicitly self-attributes the cause so it isn't filed.

findings.title: Customer reports no bugs or friction with the product
findings.description: Gordon states the tool works fine for his day-to-day use (logging in, finding sessions) and explicitly declines to offer any bug report, describing himself as not a power user. No defect or missing capability is identified.
findings.quote: It does what it does. I log in, I find my sessions, it works. I'm not a power user, I'm not going to give you a bug report.
findings.severity_reason: No issue raised; purely affirmative feedback with no actionable content.
findings.match_note: No matching catalogue issue; explicit statement that there is nothing to report.

findings.title: Positive feedback on already-shipped dark mode / mobile UI update
findings.description: Gordon notices the mobile app looks different and asks about it; Maya confirms recent updates including dark mode. Gordon responds only with appreciation ('my eyes thank you') and states that's the extent of his feedback — not a request for any change.
findings.quote: Dark mode, nice. My eyes thank you. That's the extent of my feedback.
findings.severity_reason: Cosmetic compliment on a feature already shipped (PROJ-102); no request or defect to act on.
findings.match_note: Corresponds to PROJ-102 (Dark mode, shipped 4.2) but customer is not asking for anything — pure positive feedback, so not filed as shipped_feature.

findings.title: Second location (Fort Collins) opening — future account/business context, not a product ask
findings.description: Gordon mentions Thistle Brewing is opening a second location in Fort Collins, with groundbreaking in the fall and staffing planned for early next year. This is account/business news relevant to future onboarding, not a current product defect or feature request; no immediate product action is requested.
findings.quote: Thank you. It's terrifying and exciting. Groundbreaking's in the fall, we'd staff up early next year.
findings.severity_reason: Business/account information, not a product defect or feature request.
findings.match_note: Not a product topic; noted for account context only, no matching catalogue issue.
